consensus_summary: Stone primarily identifies Jesus Christ as the rejected, living cornerstone and sure foundation; believers are also living stones in God’s spiritual house. Daniel’s stone is commonly associated with Christ, God’s kingdom, or both.
book_summary: Stone identifies a person functioning as a member of God’s building or kingdom: Christ is the rejected living Stone and chief cornerstone, his people are living stones aligned under him, and Daniel’s stone is Christ as head of the world-filling kingdom.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ as the cornerstone, with believers secondarily identified as living stones built upon him.
book_core_identification: Christ as the chief cornerstone and his people as living stones within the same divine building or kingdom.
boundary_disagreement: No material boundary disagreement. The book integrates the consensus’s primary Christological identification and its standard living-stones alternative into one building-member category. Its identification of Daniel’s stone specifically with Christ as kingdom-head selects one established Christian reading without replacing the consensus core.
material_contradiction: None. The book does not deny that the stone represents Christ, believers, or the divine kingdom-building motif recognized by the consensus.
rationale: After reducing both readings to their core, they identify the same referents and relationship: Christ is the foundational cornerstone, and believers are stones incorporated into the structure under him. The book’s generic wording, “a person as a building member,” is an abstraction covering these same cases rather than a materially broader symbolic extension. Its treatment of Daniel combines the commonly recognized Christological and kingdom readings.
strongest_objection: Daniel 2 explicitly interprets the stone’s triumph in terms of God’s kingdom, not expressly as Christ personally; therefore the claim that the stone is Christ as the kingdom’s Head is inferential. This does not undermine the directly supported cornerstone and living-stones identifications.
